title: Exclusive time of functions
label: idb-list
statement: A single-threaded program logs `"id:start:t"` when a function starts (at the beginning of tick t) and `"id:end:t"` when it finishes (at the end of tick t). Functions can call each other and themselves. Return each function's **exclusive time** — time running, not counting time spent in functions it called.
provenance: **InterviewDB-listed.** LeetCode 636 is on the LinkedIn list you supplied from InterviewDB. No candidate report of this exact question was found in the research passes — the evidence is that the list names it. On that list it uses the same pattern as InterviewDB Q6, Q7. A stack over a log of start/end events. Shares Q6’s nesting discipline and Q7’s time-ordering, without the concurrency.

stages.title: Time per function
stages.say: From start/end logs of a single-threaded program, return each function's exclusive running time.
stages.require: Implement `ExclusiveTime.Compute(n, logs)`. "start" begins at the start of tick t; "end" finishes at the end of tick t. Time spent in a called function does not count for the caller.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: A single-threaded program logs `"id:start:t"` when a function starts (at the beginning of tick t) and `"id:end:t"` when it finishes (at the end of tick t). Functions can call each other and themselves. Return each function's **exclusive time** — time running, not counting time spent in functions it called.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Is "end" inclusive of tick t? (Yes — that is the +1.)
- Are the logs well formed and in time order? (Yes.)
- Can a function call itself? (Yes — each call is a stack entry.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Whoever is on top of the call stack owns the CPU. Keep a stack of running ids and `prev`, the first tick not yet charged. On a start, charge the current top for t − prev and push. On an end, charge the top for t − prev + 1 (end is inclusive), pop, and set prev to t + 1.

learn.title: 4 · Approach

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- Off-by-one on the inclusive end.
- Charging the caller for the callee's time.
- Storing per-function start times instead of per-call, which breaks on recursion.
